title: Share the Cookie Bags Fairly

concept.title: Keep the best answer found, and cut every branch that cannot beat it
body: There are `n` bags of cookies and `k` children. A bag is given **whole** to one child. The *unfairness* of a distribution is the largest number of cookies one child gets, and we want it as small as possible. This is an **optimisation** problem: the search tries all ways to give the bags, but it keeps a variable `best` with the smallest unfairness found so far and cuts a branch as soon as it cannot improve it.

The test `kids[j] + cookies[i] >= best[0]` is a **bound**: this child would already have as many cookies as the best answer so far, so the branch cannot lead to a better answer. It becomes strong when `best` is good early, which is why the bags are given from the biggest to the smallest. Children who currently have the same amount are interchangeable, so only one of them is tried.

statement: There are `n` bags with the given numbers of cookies and `k` children. Every bag is given whole to one child (a child may get several bags or none). The *unfairness* is the largest total that one child gets. Print the smallest possible unfairness.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` numbers of cookies.

examples.note: The children can get 8 + 15 + 8 = 31 and 10 + 20 = 30: the best unfairness is 31.

hints: Give the bags one by one to a child; keep the totals of the children.
Remember the best unfairness found so far and skip a child whose total plus the bag would not beat it.
Give the bigger bags first, and try only one of several children with the same total.

starter.python:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
cookies = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: The bags go from the biggest to the smallest to a child; a child is skipped if another child with the same total was tried, or if the new total could not beat the best unfairness found so far. A complete distribution updates the best value.
solution.complexity: Time O(k^n) worst case but small with the pruning (n <= 8), space O(n).

code.python:
def distribute(cookies, i, kids, best):
    if i == len(cookies):
        best[0] = min(best[0], max(kids))
        return
    seen = set()
    for j in range(len(kids)):
        if kids[j] in seen or kids[j] + cookies[i] >= best[0]:
            continue
        seen.add(kids[j])
        kids[j] += cookies[i]
        distribute(cookies, i + 1, kids, best)
        kids[j] -= cookies[i]

n, k = map(int, input().split())
cookies = list(map(int, input().split()))

cookies.sort(reverse=True)
best = [sum(cookies) + 1]
distribute(cookies, 0, [0] * k, best)
print(best[0])
